3 DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Challenging common judgment and award dated 30.11.2015 passed by Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kalaburagi (for short 'Commissioner') in ECA.no.164/2014, these appeals are filed.
2. MFA.no.200631/2016 is filed by insurer challenging finding of Commissioner regarding occurrence of incident in course of and out of employment and consequently finding on liability.
While MFA.no.200734/2016 is filed by claimants challenging award regarding monthly income and rate of interest awarded.

3. Smt.Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel for insurer submitted that claim petition was filed alleging that NC: 2023:KHC-K:6465 on 22.06.2011, Prakash (workman) was employed as driver of Lorry bearing registration no.AAT/2874 belonging to respondent no.1 (employer) insured with respondent no.2 (insurer).
It was submitted that said workman was found dead in cabin of vehicle at Wadi Naka within limits of Kalbhor Police Station.
Claim petition was filed under provisions of Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, (for short 'E.C. Act') against employer and insurer.

It was submitted that insurer opposed petition specifically denying occurrence of incident in course of and out of employment and there was no causal connection between death and employment and therefore, it was not liable to pay compensation.
4. It was submitted that in order to establish causal connection, claimants merely produced complaint, certified copy of complainant's affidavit, certified copy of PM report and driving licence.
Ex.P3 - PM report would not indicate final conclusion regarding cause of death.
It was submitted that since no fracture or other injuries were NC: 2023:KHC-K:6465 noted, there was no basis for Commissioner to presume death was in course of employment.

Hence, following substantial question of law arose for consideration "whether Commissioner erred in concluding about occurrence of incident in course of and out of employment?".
5.
On other hand, S.G.Patil Okaly, learned counsel for claimants sought to oppose insurer's appeal and for allowing claimants' appeal.
It was submitted that there was no dispute about workman being employed as driver.
Vehicle was found at Wadi Naka with workman inside its cabin.
Complaint filed by employee of transport company would reveal that on receiving information about workman lying unconscious in cabin of Lorry, he checked and found workman dead.

It was submitted that when there was no other incident or pre-incident ailment suffered by workman that would have contributed for cause of death, Commissioner was justified in holding that incident occurred during course of and out of employment.

Insofar as appeal for enhancement, it was submitted that though claimants stated that deceased was earning Rs.6,000/- per month and Rs.60/- per day as bhatta and incident occurred on 22.06.2011, determination of monthly income of deceased by Commissioner at Rs.6,000/- would be contrary to amended Section 4 of E.C. Act.

It was further submitted that without any specific reason,
Commissioner awarded interest at 6% per annum from one month after date of accident, which Kavita W/O Late Praksh Raghame And Ors vs Manik Reddy And Anr on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133530029/
4 would be contrary to Section 4A(3)(a) of E.C. Act.

sentences.text:
Therefore, following substantial question of law arose for consideration:
"Whether assessment of monthly income and award of interest were contrary to provisions of W.C. Act?"
7.

From above submission, since employer is in appeal challenging finding of Commissioner regarding occurrence of death in course of and out of employment and claimants in appeal challenging finding regarding NC: 2023:KHC-K:6465 monthly income and interest

, following substantial questions of law would arise for consideration:
i.
Whether finding of Commissioner regarding occurrence of incident in course of and out of employment calls for interference?
ii. Whether determination of monthly income by Commissioner is contrary to Section 4(1) of W.C. Act?
iii. Whether award of interest at 6% was contrary to Section 4A(3)(a) of W.C. Act?
8. Insofar as substantial question of law no.(i):
Admittedly, workman was found dead inside cabin of Lorry, in which he was employed as driver.
Said Lorry was parked at Manjari blue Shewaladi Naka while in transit.

Though there is no dispute about fact that vehicle was stationary and had not met with any accident, complaint would reveal that complainant had received intimation from owner of vehicle about workman lying unconscious in vehicle.
Incident having occurred while workman was 'in course of employment', therefore cannot be disputed.

Insofar as occurrence of incident during out of employment,
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Jyothi Ademma v/s Plant Engineer, Nellore Thermal Station and Anr., reported in 2006 ACJ 2165, has stated that there should be some causal connection between incident and death.

entities.text: Jyothi Ademma v/s Plant Engineer, Nellore Thermal Station and Anr., reported in 2006 ACJ 2165
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "6. Under section 3(1) it has to be established that there was some causal connection between the death of the workman and his employment.

If the workman dies a natural result of the disease which he was suffering or while suffering from a particular disease he dies of that disease as a result of wear and tear, of the employment no liability would be fixed upon the employer.

But if the employment is a contributory cause or has accelerated the death, or if the death was due not only to the disease but also the disease coupled with the employment, then it can be said that death arose out of the employment and the employer would be liable."

sentences.text: It is settled position that burden to establish death was out of employment would be on claimants Though from Ex.P3 - PM report, final cause of death is awaiting chemical analysis, PM report would reveal that workman did not suffer any fractures but there was congestion in meninges and brain matter was edematous.
It is also seen that even lungs were edematous.
These would provide causal connection.
In absence of any proof regarding workman suffering from pre-incident ailment presumption has to be drawn that death was caused due to stress and strain of driving heavy motor vehicle.
Since finding of Commissioner is based upon some material and is finding of fact, same cannot be treated has giving rise to substantial question of law.
Consequently, substantial question of law no.(i) is answered in negative.

10. Insofar as substantial question of law no.(ii):
Incident has occurred on 22.06.2011, which is after date of Notification no.S.O.1258 (E) issued by Central Government notifying Rs.8,000/- as income for purposes - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6465 of Sub-Section (1) of Section 4 of E.C. Act with effect from 31.05.2010. Taking Rs.6,000/- as monthly income by Commissioner would thus be contrary to amended Section 4(1) of E.C. Act.,

Therefore, Rs.8,000/- has to be considered and award re-assessed as follows:
Rs.8,000/- X 50% X 181.37 = Rs.7,49,480/-.
Hence, substantial question of law no.(ii) is answered as above.
11.
Insofar as interest

, Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Shobha and others vs. The Chairman,
Vithalrao Shinde Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana Limited and others, reported in AIR OnLine 2022 SC 314, has held that in case of claims under Employee's Compensation Act, interest payable would be at 12% from date of incident.
